answer: In the nebula data market, agents forecast the next tide's lowest level, its nadir, for a randomly assigned gauge. Before readings arrive, each agent commits a forecast and stakes a bond; signed gauge records later score accuracy. Rewards are capped per gauge and round, and identical submissions share that cap, so aliases cannot create extra revenue. To profit across ten gauges, an attacker needs ten useful forecasts and ten bonds, with wrong answers risking loss. Spoofed sensors or shared models can distort scores, so rotate gauges, publish raw readings and allow appeals.
